input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "preservation",
 "diagnosis": "The outer invariant u == Factorial(r) is not shown to be preserved. After the inner loop Dafny only knows its invariant (v == Factorial(r) && u == s * Factorial(r)) plus !(s < r + 1), i.e. s >= r + 1, so it cannot conclude s == r + 1 and hence u == (r+1) * Factorial(r) == Factorial(r+1). The inner loop invariant is missing the upper bound s <= r + 1 (holds initially since s = 1 <= r + 1 and is maintained since s < r + 1 before increment)."}
EOF
sed -i 's/      invariant v == Factorial(r) \&\& u == s \* Factorial(r);/      invariant s <= r + 1;\n&/' program.dfy
sed -n 19,24p program.dfy; dafny verify program.dfy

content.text: Verification passes. The only thing left is the old-style semicolon warnings, which make the exit code nonzero. I'll remove those semicolons so the run is clean.

input.command: sed -i -E 's/^(\s*(requires|ensures|invariant) .*);$/\1/' program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy; echo exit=$?

content.text:
Dafny now verifies `program.dfy` (3 verified, 0 errors, exit code 0).

**What went wrong:** the outer invariant `u == Factorial(r)` (line 17) couldn't be shown to hold after each pass of the outer loop. The real gap was in the inner loop. When it ends, Dafny only knew its invariant `u == s * Factorial(r)` and that the guard was false, which means `s >= r + 1`. It had no upper bound on `s`, so it couldn't conclude `s == r + 1`, and therefore couldn't get `u == (r+1) * Factorial(r) == Factorial(r+1)`.

**Fix:** I added `invariant s <= r + 1` to the inner loop. It holds at the start (`s = 1`) and stays true because `s` only increases while `s < r + 1`. With the bound, the loop exit gives exactly `s == r + 1`.

I also removed the trailing semicolons from the `requires`/`ensures`/`invariant` lines. Dafny 4.11 flags them as deprecated style, and those warnings were making the run exit with code 2 even though all proofs passed. The change is cosmetic.

`diagnosis.json` records this as an `invariant` / `preservation` failure.
